def repl(cwd, exe):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()

    process = subprocess.Popen([exe], cwd=cwd, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, env=env, start_new_session=True)

    transcript = bytearray()
    def read_prompt():
        segment = bytearray()
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 8
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            if select.select([master], [], [], 0.1)[0]:
                try: chunk = os.read(master, 8192)
                except OSError: break
                if not chunk: break
                transcript.extend(chunk)
                segment.extend(chunk)
                if segment.endswith(b'>>> '): return
        raise AssertionError('REPL prompt not observed: ' + segment.decode(errors='replace'))
    try:

            if not chunk: break

        assert process.returncode == 0

mapping_first_appearance_order.criterion: First excerpt or named-file component explanation; mere imports, chapter prefaces and a release metadata JSON citation are not implementation lessons.

reviewer_inspection_notes: W.7 is a project-navigation and troubleshooting lesson, not a model-quality result. The complete frozen body, inline snippet, inline shell/REPL commands, optional implementation table and error examples were covered.

All 17 table rows resolve to the claimed files/directories and numbered lessons. The criterion includes named-file explanations (for example ContextMLP, tokenizer state, read_records, cache and data generation) and does not claim that every library line is copied verbatim into every cited lesson.

For omni_products, AST comparison confirms that the mathematical forward/encoding/decoding/generation and choice calculations are present. The inlined AVModel omits config_sha256; SoundCodec omits the training-only reset_unused_training_codes; collate_av and codec_spec are helpers. This supports core-computation navigation, not a claim that the full production modules and training recipes are inlined.

The path-mention completeness scan found chapter prefaces (outside numbered sections), 19.19 release.json metadata, and 19.24 attribution to the old B input grammar. 19.24 gives a new manual adapter rather than reproducing or explaining an inference.py implementation function; none changes the stated implementation-location criterion.

No prior review, issue packet, sidecar or author verdict was read. No source, figure, checker, reading-time record or public asset was edited. Only this reviewer-owned evidence file and assigned reports are delivered.
